title: Applying for a CBS studio job
summary: Hall was asked why a jazz player on 52nd Street wanted studio work.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: And I tell you an incident. I went to CBS to apply for a job and -- as a bass player, studio --
'40s. And, well, I'd been in with Stuff Smith in Chicago, and Stuff had an engagement in California. And this particular day I read an article that they were going to hire Blacks.

That's already -- well, this is of the same period. So I came to seek this job, and first thing he wanted to know, whether I was working on 52nd Street, which was demeaning at that time. You know, why are you seeking this kind of a job when you're a jazz player? But I always thought a B flat was a B flat, wherever you use it. If you have to use it, use it.
So, well, this led up to my getting a job with --
